expl: Diwan-i-Arz was the military department of the Sultanate period, and the head of this department was called ‘Ariz-i-Mumalik’. He was responsible for the administration of military affairs. He inspected the military contingents maintained by the iqta-holders.

iii. Ushr iv. Mukta'i

expl: Kharaj, Ushr and Muqta’i indicate taxes levied on land produce, whereas Khums was not a tax on land produce; rather, Khums was war booty. Khums was obtained through plunder from the people of the enemy state during war. From this booty, 4/5 was distributed among the soldiers and the remaining 1/5 was deposited in the state treasury; however, Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad Tughlaq deposited 4/5 in the treasury and distributed the remaining 1/5 among the soldiers. Sikandar Lodi did not take any share from buried treasure.

stem: Coins-Tanka, Shashgani and Jital of Sultanate period was made of which of the following metals-
expl: The two major coins of the Sultanate period were Jital and Tanka. Iltutmish was the first Turkish ruler of the Delhi Sultanate to issue pure Arabic coins. His contribution to the currency system was the greatest among the rulers of the Delhi Sultanate because he introduced two major coins— the silver Tanka and the copper Jital. Shashgani was also a silver coin. The ratio of Tanka and Jital was 1 : 48.
Aibak constructed the mosques ‘Quwwat-ul-Islam’ in Delhi and ‘Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra’ in Ajmer. He started the construction of the Qutub Minar in Delhi, which was completed by Iltutmish.

stem: The Qutub Minar was completed by-

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/ More than one of the above

expl: The construction of the Qutub Minar was started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, and it was completed during the reign of Sultan Iltutmish. It was named ‘Qutub Minar’ after the famous Sufi saint Khwaja Qutb-ud-din Bakhtiyar Kaki. It is a circular, five-storeyed structure. During the reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq, the fourth storey suffered considerable damage; therefore, Firoz not only reconstructed the fourth storey but also got the fifth storey built. Thus, instead of four storeys, the Qutub Minar came to have five storeys, which still exist today. Sultan Ulugh Khan and Razia Sultan had no contribution to the construction of the Qutub Minar.

The ‘Alai Darwaza’ was constructed by Sultan Alauddin Khalji near the Qutub Minar. It was built using red sandstone and marble. It was completed in 1311 A.D. Like Iltutmish’s tomb, it has a large square chamber with a dome on the roof, and on each of its four walls there is an arched entrance gateway.
